content:
sara nguyen: Ran a perfetto trace from the dedicated node stack (nsys -> perfetto conversion). Kernel timeline shows big GPU stalls but most frames are hex addresses, no function names.

raj patel: ugh. were those captures done inside the runtime container or on host?

sara nguyen: inside container. repro steps: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt -o /tmp/run` then `nsys export pgs /tmp/run.nsys-rep` and convert to perfetto.

devon li: common suspects: stripped binaries, missing .build-id mapping, or CUPTI failing to provide symbols. did you see any CUPTI warnings in nsys logs?

sara nguyen: no CUPTI errors in the nsys stdout, just a few permission warnings. attached excerpt: ```
[INFO] CUPTI: Initialized
[WARN] Could not open /host/proc/1234/maps: permission denied
```

amin hariri: if proc/maps isn't readable inside the container, addr2line can't map addresses to file/line. are we bind-mounting /proc from host?

sara nguyen: not by default. we run a distroless-like image that doesn't contain debuginfo. we do bind /var/lib/runtime for models but not /proc.

raj patel: that explains it. nsys collects addresses but symbolization step (perfetto/trace-processor) needs either access to the binaries + debug files or a debugserver that resolves addresses. inside lightweight container we lack that.

devon li: quick repro suggestion: run the container with `--cap-add=SYS_PTRACE` and `-v /proc:/host_proc:ro` then set `TRACE_PROC_ROOT=/host_proc` before running convert. see if perfetto can read maps.

sara nguyen: tried mounting /proc and adding SYS_PTRACE, got better mapping for some frames but still a bunch unresolved. looked at `readelf --notes` -> build-id present on host binary but the container copy has different build-id (multi-stage artifact renaming).

amin hariri: Ah, multi-stage builds can rewrite paths or strip and re-add symbols differently. Did the pipeline use `objcopy --strip-debug` or `strip --strip-all`?

sara nguyen: our packaging step runs `strip --strip-unneeded` for smaller image. but CI also creates separate `.debug` files and runs `objcopy --only-keep-debug`. we then upload debug packages to internal dbg service, but runtime image doesn't contain them.

raj patel: That's fine if the trace processor has access to .debug files and correct build-id mapping under `/usr/lib/debug/.build-id/xx/yyy.debug`. Can you check if trace conversion step points to our debug store?

sara nguyen: trace-processor was run on the same container without network access to debug store. CI artifacts are on a different host.

devon li: Two approaches: 1) make the conversion step run in CI or in the host environment with access to debugstore, or 2) ship debug files into the container at repro time (mount or sidecar). For production debugging we prefer approach 1.

amin hariri: Also check that the build preserves build-ids when rebuilding or repackaging. If file paths inside binary were remapped during build (PATHMAP), addr2line needs a pathmap or the .debug to have matching build-id.

sara nguyen: confirmed build-id mismatch between host debugfile and container binary. root cause: our docker image re-compressed and re-labeled the ELF during packaging step (we add a small wrapper and relinker).

raj patel: Could that relinker be using `--remove-section` or some LTO step? That would change the build-id.

sara nguyen: yes the packaging tool runs `patchelf` to set rpath and then a `eu-strip --remove-section=.comment` step.

devon li: Actions: 1) stop destructive strip in packaging for a debug build variant. 2) reproduce with unstripped binary in container and mount host /proc and run converter on host. 3) add debug-store access to trace-processor pipeline.

amin hariri: Also add a small helper to the runtime that prints its own build-id at startup: `readelf -n $(which runtime) | grep -A1 "Build ID"` so traces can be correlated to artifact.

sara nguyen: added helper in a branch: prints `BUILD_ID=abcdef1234`. pushed to `perf/symbol-fix`.

trace-bot: Upload complete: /artifacts/perf/run-1768923456.nsys (size 124MB) :white_check_mark:

raj patel: thanks. next, about batching heuristics: without symbolization we couldn't confirm where KV cache eviction hotspots are. Once we get symbols, let's re-run the 60s profile with the new kernel selection flags (`--kernel-candidate=fastmem`), compare host vs container.

devon li: I'm also worried CUPTI can sometimes return truncated stack samples if guest and host driver mismatch. confirm CUDA driver versions inside container vs host kernel module.

sara nguyen: host nvidia-driver 535.61, container cuda runtime 11.8. driver mismatch possible. opening infra ticket to align images.

amin hariri: Good. For immediate debugging: 1) reproduce with unstripped image + mounted /proc; 2) run `nsys profile --sample=cpu --cuda` and `nvprof --analysis-metrics` to compare; 3) use `addr2line -e /path/to/binary 0x7f2a...` for unresolved addrs.

sara nguyen: I'm on it. scheduling a 1h debug session tomorrow 09:30 to repro with devon.

raj patel: assignable follow-ups: sara -> repro and confirm build-id fix; devon -> add debug-store access to trace-processor; amin -> infra ticket for driver alignment.

devon li: added a short script to collect debug artifacts: `collect-debug.sh` that bundles binary, .debug, /proc/<pid>/maps and uploads to internal dbg. will post link in thread.

sara nguyen: posted link: https://internal.artifacts/reports/1768923456-bundle.tar.gz

amin hariri: Ack. If we still see gaps after build-id and proc mapping fixes, next step is to run perfetto consumer on the host and use `trace_processor_shell` with `symbolize_reports()` pointing to debug dir.

raj patel: Great. thanks team. short-term workaround: for outage traces, run conversion on host with debugstore mounted. long-term: ensure packaging preserves build-id or publish mapping at release time. :thumbsup:

sara nguyen: thanks everyone. will update after tomorrow's repro. :coffee:
